title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' builds tame topology combinatorially. Here he treats the 1-dimensional model case. L is an ordered set of 'lieux' (points). The 'multiplicités' M are of two kinds. M_0 consists of the points P_x for x in L. M_1 consists of the open segments S_{a,b} for a<b. Their boundary is ∂S_{a,b} = {P_a, P_b}.

On the previous page he worked out when two multiplicities are compatible (X ≭ Y), roughly when they can be strata of one common stratification:
- they are equal;
- they are disjoint, including disjoint closures;
- a point is incident to a segment (P_x is an endpoint);
- two segments are adjacent, a<b≤a'<b'.

On this page he introduces δX, the set of vertices of X: δP_x = {x} and δS_{a,b} = {a,b}. So δX ⊂ L and card δX ∈ {1,2}. He observes a necessary condition: if X ≭ Y, then δX ∪ δY ∈ Drap(L), the set of finite totally ordered subsets (flags or chains) of L.

He then lists the possible cardinalities:
- 1: X = Y a point.
- 2: two distinct points; a point and a segment of which it is an endpoint; X = Y a segment.
- 3: a point and a segment disjoint from it (x<a or x>b); two contiguous segments S_{a,b}, S_{b,c}.
- 4: two disjoint segments.

He sums this up as: points equal or disjoint; point incident to or disjoint from a segment; segments disjoint or adjacent.

Generalization: for a flag T = {t_1<…<t_n} he defines the 'interstitial' strata of T. These are the points P_{t_i} (interstitial lieux) and the segments S_{t_i,t_{i+1}} (interstitial segments). The marginal NB notes that if card T = 1 there are no interstitial segments, flagged 'à vérifier'.

This prepares the next page's proposition. A finite family F is pairwise compatible iff δF is a flag and every element of F is an indecomposable (interstitial) stratum for δF. The maximal such family for a given T is the 'canonical figure' F_T: the stratification of [t_1,t_n] into alternating points and open intervals. In modern terms: finite compatible configurations of strata on a line are classified by finite chains, i.e. by stratified intervals or subdivisions. This is the combinatorial base case for his later study of how supports behave.
errors: The condition δX∪δY ∈ Drap(L) is (correctly) stated only as necessary. Some incompatible pairs also give a flag: overlapping segments a<a'<b<b', nested segments, or a point strictly inside a segment (a<x<b). This is why the next page adds the condition that the elements be indecomposable (interstitial) for δF. The page itself does not yet spell out these counterexamples.
The cardinality list compresses the parenthetical: '(si X,Y∈M_1 et X∥Y)' refers only to cardinal 4. Read literally, the sentence is slightly garbled, but the mathematics is right.
The marginal case card T = 1 (no interstitial segments) is consistent with the later Proposition, which requires F non-empty.

ideas.what: Vertex set δX of a point or segment stratum, and the necessary condition that a compatible pair spans a chain of L
ideas.modern_name: vertex set of a simplex in the order complex (nerve) of a poset; chains as simplices
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard combinatorial topology (order complex: folklore; Alexandroff, McCord, Quillen in a poset context)

ideas.what: Interstitial points and segments of a flag T = {t_1<…<t_n}, and the canonical figure F_T
ideas.modern_name: stratification of an interval by a finite subdivision; the 'stratified interval' or 1-truss determined by a finite linear order
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; recent formal treatment in Dorn–Douglas 'framed combinatorial topology' (trusses)

ideas.what: Classification of compatible pairs of strata on a line: equal, disjoint, incident, adjacent
ideas.modern_name: frontier condition / incidence relations in a 1-dimensional regular cell stratification
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Whitney/Thom-style stratification combinatorics; regular CW complexes)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and stratified structures only programmatically

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up an encoding of configurations of mutually compatible strata of a 1-dimensional stratified 'line' by finite flags of an ordered set, with a canonical maximal figure for each flag. Unpublished, this anticipates the combinatorial approach to stratified/tame spaces via linear orders (e.g. trusses in framed combinatorial topology). The mathematics itself is elementary.
missed.quote: si on a T ∈ Drap(L), T={t_1,…,t_n} avec t_1<…<t_n, on définira les segments interstitiels de T … P_{t_i} sont appelés les lieux interstitiels
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence that Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs' pursued tame topology through combinatorial base cases of exactly this type. It is of interest to historians of tame and stratified topology, not as a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine combinatorics of points and intervals in an ordered set, a base case of the stratification bookkeeping. It is correct but elementary; only its place in the unpublished Analysis situs project is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: 'Dnp(L)' / 'Dnp[?](L)' should read 'Drap(L)' (flags), consistent with the next page; likewise 'Disp' on the previous page is probably 'Drap'.
'en dirait par card égal à 1' is likely 'en distinguant par card égal à 1' or similar ('… de cardinal égal à 1').
The summary brace reads approximately: 'lieux égaux ou disjoints / lieu incident à un segment, ou disjoint des segments / segments disjoints, segments adjacents'.
Marginal NB: approximately 'Si card T = 1, il n'y a pas de segment interstitiel (à vérifier)', rather than 'segment interstitiel vide'.
'plus exactement' is probably 'ou encore' / 'ou celui de X,Y∈M_1, comme S_{a,b}, S_{b,c} avec a<b<c (segments contigus)'.
'Ainsi trois possibilités' is plausibly 'Ainsi trois possibilités' or 'Au total, possibilités'; the image suggests 'Au total, possibilités'.
